clue.text: Pincers from lobsters primarily found between jetties

indicators.note: something found between two things sits inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: piers are jetties projecting into the sea

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the creatures is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A seaside scene: lobsters scuttling between the jetties, claws first.
explanation.walkthrough: The lobster's pincers make the definition look like part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a gripping hand tool, and pincers is another name for such a tool.

clue.text: Fixed position with upcoming young artist

parts.note: one's station is one's position or post

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Y is a standard abbreviation for young
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A promising young painter is given a permanent spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the young artist part is turned upward; the position stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stationary is not moving, held in one place, which is what fixed describes.

clue.text: Sorts out certain matter arising

parts.note: if you are clear about something you are certain

indicators.note: arising means getting up, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: pus is the matter discharged from an infection

explanation.surface: Someone settles a definite issue that has come up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like an issue to deal with; here it is the medical sense, the yellow stuff in a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a problem is to resolve or tidy it, which is what sorting it out means.

clue.text: Little bit of pudding

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small or trivial amount
second meaning: a layered dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.surface: Someone asks for just a small helping of dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pudding means dessert in general; this one is the cold layered sweet with jelly and custard.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is both a trivial small amount and a classic British layered cold dessert.

clue.text: Concrete counter absorbs spilled gin

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so the counter holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a table or counter is a flat working surface

indicators.note: a spilled drink ends up in a mess, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bar top soaks up a spilt measure of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' looks like a building material describing the counter; it is the adjective meaning real.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangible can be touched and is real, the adjectival sense of concrete as opposed to abstract.

clue.text: Lazy and idle, not working around noon

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the single letter
the words are worked over, kneaded into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A slacker who does no work even at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' reads as part of the definition alongside 'Lazy', but it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent describes someone who avoids effort and exertion, a direct synonym for lazy.

clue.text: Fit for Charlton's team?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: physically strong and in good condition
second meaning: the football club of Charlton in south-east London

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a player is in shape to play for Charlton.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlton Athletic is an English football club based in south-east London; the question mark flags the club name used as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic describes a sporty, strong body, and it is also the second half of the London football club's name.

clue.text: Turn up wearing reservists' old clothing

indicators.note: something being worn is put on, so it sits inside what wears it

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Army reservists show up in outdated uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' suggests arriving; it splits into a turn and the upward signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer garment of ancient Roman citizens, so it is clothing from long ago.

clue.text: Pretty sharp, heading off

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: acute means keen or sharp, as in an acute mind

explanation.surface: Something quite keen is setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty sharp' reads as 'fairly sharp', with pretty as an adverb; it is really the adjective meaning attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute and pretty are both adjectives for something attractive or charming to look at.

clue.text: Agreed it's strange, entering study when retired

indicators.note: something entering a room goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the room is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat at home
odd means strange

explanation.surface: Someone concedes it is odd that they went into the study after going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is a gesture of assent, so having nodded means having agreed.

clue.text: Direct view round painting retrospective

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the view goes around the other piece

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests reading the word backwards

parts.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A gallery visitor heads straight to see a painter's retrospective exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painting retrospective' sounds like an exhibition looking back over an artist's career.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight and direct are synonyms describing a route or answer without detours or evasion.

clue.text: Poor American threesome busk stripped to get famous

parts.note: poor health is ill health
US is short for American
a trio is a group of three

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, the word keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Three hard-up Americans play music in the street, hoping for fame.
explanation.walkthrough: To busk is to perform in the street for money; 'stripped' takes off its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Illustrious describes someone renowned and highly distinguished, which is a stronger form of being famous.

clue.text: Run on vintage junk for restoration

definitions.note: noun defining a verb form; renovating is the act of restoration

indicators.note: to junk something is to scrap it, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dealer touts old vintage junk as ripe for doing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' looks like the vintage stuff itself; it is the instruction to scrap the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Renovating a building means restoring it to good condition, the activity called restoration.

clue.text: Wet suit bafflingly punctures again

indicators.note: to puncture is to pierce, so these letters go into the middle of the other word

parts.note: more can mean again, as in once more

indicators.note: something baffling is confusing, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diver's wetsuit mysteriously keeps getting holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet suit' reads as one diving garment, but wet is the definition and suit is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The wet, used as a noun, means dampness or water, which is what moisture is.

clue.text: Naive revolutionary married unknown seer and died

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: wed means married
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x
an eye is what sees
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: An innocent rebel marries a mystery prophet and then dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer' suggests a prophet; here it is the organ that sees.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy-eyed describes someone sentimental and innocently trusting, so it fits naive as an adjective.

clue.text: Learnt about new source of light

indicators.note: turned about, the letters face a new way and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone has found out about a fresh way to light things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a protective case, a device giving illumination.

clue.text: Insubstantial online article's true

parts.note: E- as in e-mail stands for electronic, online
the definite article
real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a flimsy internet piece is accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online article' looks like a web post; it splits into two pieces, the electronic prefix and the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means airy and delicate, as if not made of solid matter, so it is insubstantial.

clue.text: Endorse program range

parts.note: an app is a computer program
to range is to wander or rove

explanation.surface: Someone gives the thumbs-up to a software product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a noun, a product range; it is the verb meaning wander.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve of something is to give it your official backing, which is to endorse it.

clue.text: Times contains a very easy cut-out as always to express one's opinion

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the times go around the following letters

parts.note: hours are set times, as in opening hours
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: with its inside cut out, the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
ay is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A newspaper offers an easy cut-out coupon so readers can always give their views.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the newspaper the surface suggests; here it is just hours. Ay, meaning ever, survives in phrases like 'for ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have your say is an idiom for stating your view or getting your opinion heard.

clue.text: New university students given education

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
the NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
Ed is the abbreviation for education

explanation.surface: Fresh undergraduates are given some teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused has never been worn or handled, so it is still brand new.

clue.text: Rush to animal park before the end of term

indicators.note: coming before means placed first, so the park leads and the other letter follows

parts.note: a zoo is a park where animals are kept

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Families hurry to the zoo before school term finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To zoom is to move very fast, so it is a synonym for rush as a verb.

clue.text: Lump of ice in cucumber gin

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, spanning them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An ice cube floats in a gin with cucumber, the fashionable garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: Hendrick's style gin is served with cucumber, so the ice belongs in the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg is short for iceberg, a huge mass of floating ice, so a lump of ice.

clue.text: Make too much of charge on six deliveries?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Someone complains of overcharging for a delivery service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the charge after the six deliveries. Deliveries are balls bowled in cricket, six to an over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate something is to value it above its worth, making too much of it.

clue.text: Student's university union holds vote on railway extravagance

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so the vote sits within

parts.note: L is a learner, the crossword student, as on British L-plates
U is the abbreviation for university
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper
U is the abbreviation for union
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A student union backs a vote about lavish spending on the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: The vote sits between the two single letters for university and union.
explanation.definitionFit: A luxury is something expensive and inessential, an indulgence or extravagance.

clue.text: Condition of Russian fighter's low grade after downpour

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
a downpour is heavy rain
E is a low exam grade

explanation.surface: A Russian soldier's poor showing follows a soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the grade behind the downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring headache, a medical condition.

clue.text: US agent returned to kill guard

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the agent is read backwards

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent, such as an FBI officer
to end a life is to kill

explanation.surface: An American federal agent comes back to carry out a hit on a bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to protect from harm, which is what guarding someone means.
